cim: Pentagon mandates artificial intelligence training for cyber workforce
cim_eredeti: Pentagon mandates artificial intelligence training for cyber workforce
szoveg_eredeti:
The Department of Defense is implementing mandatory artificial intelligence training for its entire cybersecurity workforce to address evolving digital threats, according to Defensescoop.

Mark Gorak, the principal director for resources and analysis in the Office of the Chief Information Officer, announced the initiative during the FedTalks summit. The Pentagon aims to integrate AI as a foundational skill to counter adversaries who use algorithms for automated reconnaissance and social engineering. This shift coincides with a transition toward skills-based hiring, where candidates are evaluated through practical testing in cyber ranges rather than relying solely on resumes or credentials.

The department currently faces a shortage of 24,000 personnel within its 240,000-member cyber workforce. To bridge this gap, officials have expanded to 79 defined cybersecurity roles, up from 76 last year. Beyond AI training and performance-based assessments, the Pentagon is pursuing rotational programs with private industry to bolster recruitment. These efforts reflect a broader strategy to modernize the defense cyber apparatus against sophisticated global threats. The department plans to discuss these workforce challenges further during a summit scheduled for April 7 to 9 at the National Defense University.
